answer: Latency Ledger Registration. Each identity must complete a unique timed task sequence whose delays are measured at the network edge, with results signed by a haven of independent timestampers. Registration is rejected if any two identities share timing fingerprints. An attacker pays real elapsed time per identity plus the cost of distinct network paths; bulk creation fails because parallel tasks collide on timing signatures. A violet flag marks collisions, and yarrow-salted challenges rotate to prevent precomputation.
